questions.stem: Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years. It is useful for dating objects up to approximately how old?
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 dating is useful for dating organic remains up to about 50,000 years old. Beyond this, the amount of carbon-14 remaining is too small to measure accurately. For older rocks, uranium dating (half-life ~4.5 billion years) is used instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT affect the half-life of a radioactive isotope?

options.text: All of the above do not affect half-life

questions.explanation: Half-life is a fixed property of a radioactive isotope and is not affected by any external conditions, including temperature, pressure, or chemical state. This is because radioactive decay is a nuclear process, and conditions that affect electron behaviour have no influence on the nucleus.
